nodes.title: A model call is asked for
nodes.say: The caller names an operation, such as chat completion, and the multi LLM service checks that a provider is registered for it before building the request.

nodes.title: Queued or sent direct
nodes.say: When the shared dispatch queue is installed, the stream becomes a job with provider permits, quotas and a cloud cap; otherwise it goes straight to the router.

nodes.title: Operation becomes a profile
nodes.say: The magicllm router looks the operation up in llm-router.yaml's operation mapping, honours any pinned profile or provider, then applies that profile's defaults and capability checks.

nodes.title: Local or remote model
nodes.say: Each profile names its model: one running on this machine through Ollama, or a hosted one across the internet. Choose where this call goes.
nodes.decidedBy: the resolved profile's provider in llm-router.yaml (provider: ollama is local; everything else is remote), with privacy.processing.mode: cloud switching when_cloud arms to their remote profiles

options.label: Remote model
options.say: The profile names a hosted vendor, so the call leaves the machine through that vendor's adapter.

options.label: Local model (Ollama)
options.say: The profile names Ollama, so the call stays on this machine and goes to the local Ollama server.

nodes.title: Ollama on port 11434
nodes.say: The Ollama adapter posts to the local server on port 11434, keeping the model resident for a while, and returns one complete answer rather than streaming tokens.

nodes.title: Hosted providers
nodes.say: Magician speaks to ten hosted vendors, each through its own adapter and A P I. Pick a provider to follow the request there.
nodes.decidedBy: the profile's provider field in llm-router.yaml, matched to one registered adapter at boot (harness-<engine> custom providers map to the subscription CLI adapter)

options.label: OpenAI
options.say: The most used provider in the shipped router config, and the one chat completion maps to by default.

options.label: Anthropic
options.say: Claude models over Anthropic's Messages API.

options.label: Gemini
options.say: Google's Gemini models over the generative language API.

options.label: DeepSeek
options.say: DeepSeek models through DeepSeek's Anthropic compatible endpoint.

options.label: MiniMax
options.say: MiniMax models over a chat completions style API.

options.label: xAI Grok
options.say: Grok models over xAI's Responses API.

options.label: Sarvam
options.say: Sarvam's Indic first models for Indian languages.

options.label: Yutori N1
options.say: Yutori's vision and computer use model for screenshot heavy steps.

options.label: OpenRouter
options.say: One gateway to many vendors; supported in code, though no shipped profile selects it.

options.label: Subscription CLI
options.say: An installed Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Antigravity or Pi CLI used as a plain text model.

nodes.title: OpenAI: chat or responses
nodes.say: The OpenAI adapter picks Chat Completions or the Responses API for each request from the profile's API mode, then streams through that sub adapter.

nodes.title: Anthropic Messages API
nodes.say: The Anthropic adapter posts to the Messages API and streams text, thinking blocks and tool call fragments back as the server events arrive.

nodes.title: Google Gemini
nodes.say: The Gemini adapter calls Google's generative language API without token streaming, so the router receives the whole answer as one final piece.

nodes.title: DeepSeek
nodes.say: The DeepSeek adapter wraps the Anthropic messages adapter, aimed at DeepSeek's Anthropic compatible endpoint, and streams its replies through that inner adapter.

nodes.title: MiniMax
nodes.say: The MiniMax adapter speaks a chat completions style API at MiniMax and streams text and tool call deltas back to the router.

nodes.title: xAI Grok
nodes.say: The xAI adapter wraps the OpenAI Responses adapter, aimed at xAI's endpoint, refuses chat mode, and streams Grok's replies through it.

nodes.title: Sarvam
nodes.say: The Sarvam adapter is its own chat completions transport for Sarvam's Indic first models, handling their quirks, and streams the reply back.

nodes.title: Yutori N1
nodes.say: The Yutori adapter sends chat completions to the N1 vision and computer use model, and returns one complete answer rather than a token stream.

nodes.title: OpenRouter
nodes.say: The OpenRouter adapter sends chat completions to OpenRouter, which fronts many vendors, and returns the complete answer in one final piece.

nodes.title: Subscription CLI as a model
nodes.say: A harness profile flattens the request into one prompt, runs the installed CLI with a curated environment, and parses its printed answer as plain text.

nodes.title: Fallback profile
nodes.say: On a non streaming call, a failed provider hands the request to its profile's fallback profile, with loop detection; a streaming call has no fallback hop.

nodes.title: Retry and cooldown
nodes.say: Queued calls retry in place with backoff, then requeue; a stream gets one attempt, and its failure puts that provider into a cooldown.

nodes.title: Answer flows back
nodes.say: Tokens and tool call fragments flow back through a channel, and a final done piece carries the full response, stamped with its trace receipt.

nodes.title: Ask for a decision client
nodes.say: Before building any prompt or touching the socket, the caller asks the decision host whether the current mode lets this engine use the Decision Engine.

nodes.title: Decision engine on or off
nodes.say: The Decision Engine can be switched on, so a structured model weighs in, or off, so the caller carries on alone. Choose one.
nodes.decidedBy: decision.mode in magician-config.yaml (all_engines, magician_only or off); the supervisor also only starts the engine when decision_engine_enabled is set and the binary is installed

options.label: On
options.say: The mode allows this engine, so the caller sends the step to the Decision Engine.

options.label: Off
options.say: No client comes back, so the caller returns at once to its own native model path.

nodes.title: Build the action request
nodes.say: The decision rail packs the goal, instructions, recent evidence, offered tools, remaining plan and processing locality into one action request.

nodes.title: Over the Unix socket
nodes.say: The engine client posts the request as HTTP over a Unix socket to the separate engine process, and rejects any reply whose snapshot does not match.

nodes.title: Decision Engine receives it
nodes.say: The engine serves the action and decide routes on its socket, picks the local or cloud runtime for the request's locality, and runs the action driver.

nodes.title: Frame the next-action question
nodes.say: The action driver validates the request, grounds candidate calls in the offered tools, and asks a next action question with a planner option added.

nodes.title: Which models may serve
nodes.say: From decision-engine.yaml, each operation gets a pinned model or a tier, local models below the memory floor drop out, and private steps refuse remote models locally.

nodes.title: Walk the model route
nodes.say: The runtime tries the route's models in order, skipping misfits, moving on when a model is unavailable, and keeping the first answer that clears its thresholds.

nodes.title: Decision models
nodes.say: Three structured models can answer: the hosted Jev, or laya and Kev running on this machine. Pick the model to follow.
nodes.decidedBy: the operation's model, tier or routing in decision-engine.yaml (tool_action_judge pins jev; tiers small: [laya], large: [kev-4b, jev]), filtered by locality and local_min_memory_gb

options.label: Hosted Jev
options.say: TypeSafe's hosted Jev model, reached over the System One wire with an API key.

options.label: Local laya
options.say: The small laya encoder running inside the engine on this machine's GPU or CPU.

options.label: Local Kev
options.say: Kev, a larger local model with long context and many options, for the large tier.

nodes.title: Jev answers remotely
nodes.say: The System One adapter posts the typed question to TypeSafe's endpoint, with timeouts and retries, and reads back the chosen option and its confidence.

nodes.title: laya answers locally
nodes.say: The laya adapter runs the model inside the engine process, on Apple Silicon through MLX or on the CPU through ONNX, and scores each option.

nodes.title: Kev answers locally
nodes.say: The Kev adapter runs a local language model with a pointer head that reads long state and points at one option, through MLX or ONNX.

nodes.title: Confidence gate
nodes.say: The driver accepts the pick only above the next action confidence threshold, then a review question checks the evidence is sufficient and the call applies.

nodes.title: The engine's verdict
nodes.say: The engine can pick a call, ask for a planner, reject the request, or step aside. Choose a verdict to see what follows.
nodes.decidedBy: the action driver's checks: request validation, whether tool_action_judge is enabled, and the thresholds in decision-engine.yaml (next_action_confidence, evidence_sufficient, action_applicable)

options.label: Pick a call
options.say: The model chose a grounded call with enough confidence, so the engine authorizes that exact tool call.

options.label: Ask for a planner
options.say: The model was unsure or asked for planning, so a generative model must propose the next steps.

options.label: Reject
options.say: The request or a planner proposal failed validation, so no tool may run.

options.label: Step aside
options.say: The action operation is switched off in the engine, so it answers disabled before any model runs.

nodes.title: Execute this call
nodes.say: The engine returns an execute verdict with the chosen call, its confidence, and the rest of the plan to carry into the next step.

nodes.title: Ask a planner
nodes.say: The engine writes planner instructions and a prompt; the caller runs its own model with them, and the engine validates the proposed first step afterwards.

nodes.title: Rejected
nodes.say: A contract mismatch, an invalid request or an invalid planner proposal becomes a rejected verdict, and no tool is dispatched from it.

nodes.title: Step aside
nodes.say: When the engine has no enabled action operation, it answers disabled, which tells the caller to carry on with its ordinary model path.

nodes.title: Verdict back in Magician
nodes.say: Back in Magician, the rail records model usage and health, then turns the verdict into run this call, ask the planner, bypass, or an error.
